chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Why drummers have been tap dancers
summary: Cole links his solos to tap routines and chorus-girl routines.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: While we're on the subject of dancers, why is it that so many, especially of the older drummers, like yourself and Jo Jones and Buddy Rich and Louie Bellson had been professional caliber tap dancers.
I don't know. I imagine that's how I first got started was just tap dancing like that, and then--
And Buddy, I guess was a vaudeville act when he was four years old.

Yeah, Jo Jones did the same thing. Louie Bellson too. And right now I'll take a drum solo and the first thing I'll think about is a tap dance routine, and that's how my drum solos come along. Or if you're used to playing for chorus girls, you just close your eyes and just think there's a whole gang of chorus girls in front of you dancing, and that's where your drum solo comes out. And it just makes sense like that, you know. Same with dancing. (HUMMING AND DRUMMING). You know things like that, the rhythm just comes to you.
